abstract: Maintains physical route condition logs, bridge weight tolerances, and viaduct load certifications
system_message:
You are Civil infrastructure engineer (CIE). The Civil infrastructure engineer (CIE) maintains physical route condition logs, bridge weight tolerances, and viaduct load certifications, and oversees seismic resilience evaluations across all candidate corridors.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Seismic resilience evaluation（SEIS）
information_points.content:
CIE-SEIS-N2W：The Inland waterway barge corridor has a seismic peak ground acceleration threshold of 0.15 g at critical viaduct and bridge foundation subgrades.
CIE-SEIS-AGT：The Direct freight rail corridor has a seismic peak ground acceleration threshold of 0.25 g at critical viaduct and bridge foundation subgrades.
CIE-SEIS-1MR：The Dedicated highway hazmat bypass has a seismic peak ground acceleration threshold of 0.35 g at critical viaduct and bridge foundation subgrades.

information_points.title: Maintains physical route condition logs, bridge weight tolerances, and viaduct load certifications（STRUCT）
information_points.content:
CIE-STRUCT-YP9：For the Direct freight rail corridor, bridge structural capacity certification holds across all highway bridges, railway trestles, or canal aqueducts on the corridor for gross combination vehicle loads exceeding 80 metric tons.
CIE-STRUCT-MK2：For the Inland waterway barge corridor, bridge structural capacity certification holds across all highway bridges, railway trestles, or canal aqueducts on the corridor for gross combination vehicle loads exceeding 80 metric tons.
CIE-STRUCT-RXG：For the Dedicated highway hazmat bypass, bridge structural capacity certification does not hold across all highway bridges, railway trestles, or canal aqueducts on the corridor for gross combination vehicle loads exceeding 80 metric tons.
